issues.title: t-SNE default parameters and clarifying documentation
issues.body:
This issue is intended to trigger discussion and a decision about t-SNE default parameters and about t-SNE documentation.

Also, see issue #19510, which I believe was closed prematurely.

## Items to consider

(1) The scale of PCA initialization. At the current time, the scale of PCA initialization is whatever the PCA outputs. But, t-SNE works better when initialization is small. Consider re-scaling so that the standard deviation of the first column is 1e-4, for example:

X_embedded = X_embedded / np.std(X_embedded[:, 0]) * 1e-4

That re-scaling would give a scale approximately the same size as that of random initialization.

(2) The learning rate. Recommendation (2) in issue #19510 suggests: The learning rate is maybe too large by default in case the perplexity is large. Note that for n samples, the perplexity should be less than n, and a typical default should be in the 5-50 range. Whereas, the default in scikit-learn is 200. Consider implementing learning_rate="auto" so that we can (1) enable it by default, and (2) more importantly spread the word that users can use learning_rate="auto".

(3) The documentation. The docstrings at the class and parameter levels can be improved. For example, the class docstring says: "It is highly recommended to use another dimensionality reduction method ... to reduce the number of dimensions to a reasonable amount (e.g. 50) if the number of features is very high." According to the t-SNE author (van der Maaten), that's misleading; the amount of PCA reduction is a knob that can be used to control the amount of noise smoothing. Also note the t-SNE FAQ at https://lvdmaaten.github.io/tsne/ - the docs could link to it. A new user, especially one who does not already have a background in dimensionality reduction, is likely to be misled by our current docs.

(4) Random initialization and the global structure of the mapping. The PCA initialization gives more global structure than random initialization. But the PCA reduction can be performed in several ways, for example: (a) with the default (random) svd_solver, (b) with svd_solver="full", (c) with a svd_solver="randomized" and a specific random_state, or (d) with an external package. Our docs should say something about the benefits of using PCA initialization.

## Tasks

[x] - Pick one: (1) re-scale the initialization to 1e-4, or (2) do nothing. - See PR #20629.
[x] - Decide whether to implement learning_rate="auto". See PR #20212.
[x] - Improve the class docstring. Expand and add links to the "How to use t-SNE effectively" blog post and the FAQ.
[x] - Add a gallery example showing the effect of the perplexity parameter.
[x] - Add notes about PCA initialization to the docstrings, and mention that initialization is re-scaled when init="pca".
[ ] - Consider the suggestions about initialization and early exaggeration in the paper "Cluster-preserving dimensionality reduction for visualizing high-dimensional data" (Kobak & Linderman) and the issues referenced there.

## Additional context

See the suggestions and comments in issue #19510.

## References

- The scikit-learn t-SNE implementation: sklearn/manifold/_t_sne.py
- The t-SNE FAQ: https://lvdmaaten.github.io/tsne/
- Blog post: https://distill.pub/2016/misread-tsne/
- Issue #19510 and PR #20629, PR #20212.
